evals.prompt: F7 and F8 work in our Playwright E2E against Vite mock but do nothing in the real Tauri app on a MacBook. We only registered global shortcuts for Code::F7 and Code::F8 in Rust. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: MacBook default sends media keys (MediaRewind / MediaPlayPause), not F7/F8 scancodes; RegisterEventHotKey for Code::F7 alone misses media-key mode. Also add NSMenu accelerators on File menu items, emit menu-action to the frontend, and verify in tauri dev — Playwright mock does not reproduce macOS routing.

evals.prompt: Our Tauri macOS menu bar shows the app name, Edit, View but no File menu. We built the menu with File as the first submenu. How do we fix it?
evals.expected_output: On macOS the first submenu merges into the application menu regardless of label; put an app submenu first (About/Hide/Quit), then a separate File submenu second. Use distinct item ids if duplicating file commands in the app menu (e.g. -app suffix).

evals.prompt: Should we rely on React keydown handlers inside the WebView for F7 new-folder on macOS?
evals.expected_output: No as the only path — bare F7 often never reaches WebView in media-key mode. Use NSMenu accelerators plus tauri-plugin-global-shortcut with both F7 and MediaRewind (and F8 / MediaPlayPause for delete); keep WebView keydown as supplementary for standard-function-key mode and other platforms.

evals.prompt: tauri-plugin-global-shortcut on_shortcut for MediaPlayPause registered but delete still doesn't fire on F8. Any macOS permission gotcha?
evals.expected_output: Media keys use CGEventTap in global-hotkey; macOS may require Accessibility permission for the app. Check Rust logs for per-shortcut registration failures; media tap creation can fail silently if accessibility is denied — standard F-key registration may still succeed while media keys do not.
